paper_metadata.title: Effect of carbon nanotube content on the microstructure and mechanical properties of CNTs/TiAl alloys

The pre-alloyed powders were placed in a planetary ball mill (QM-3SP2, China) with different CNT contents after ultrasonication for 30 min.
Subsequently, WC grinding balls were placed in the tank at a mass ratio of 5:1 to the powder mixtures. The ball-milling process lasted for 12 h at a rotation speed of 250 rpm.
After drying in a vacuum drying oven (DZF-1, China) at 120 ◦ C and sifting through a 100 mesh sieve, the powder mixtures of CNTs/TiAl alloys was prepared.
The powders were heated to 1000 ◦ C at a rate of 100 ◦ C/min, maintained for 10 min, and then cooled to room temperature.

attributes.morphology: granular and banded stacked at grain boundaries

evidence.quote: A banded Ti 2 AlC structure formed by the stacked granular Ti 2 AlC phase was found at the grain boundary.
When CNTs were not added, the CNT/TiAl alloys had tiny blocky structures of α 2 / γ phases with an average grain size of approximately 60 μ m.
When the CNT content was 0.4 wt%, the microstructure also exhibited blocky morphology, with a refined grain size of approximately 32 μ m.
In the absence of CNTs, the Vickers hardness of the material was 364 HV.
At 0.4 wt% CNT content, a certain amount of Ti 2 AlC phase and a small amount of TiC phase were generated, which strengthened the alloy and increased the Vickers hardness value to 377 HV.
When the CNT content was 0.7 wt%, the contents of TiC and Ti 2 AlC phases further increased, and the Vickers hardness value reached a maximum of 384 HV.
When the CNT content was 0.4 wt%, the bending strength was 879 MPa, which is 7.1% higher than that without CNTs.

The striped Ti 2 AlC phase limited grain growth and played a role in fine-grain strengthening.

Furthermore, TiC and Ti 2 AlC phases generated by the reactions can also play a role in the second-phase strengthening as ceramic strengthening phases, which improved the bending strength of the CNTs/TiAl alloys.
